description: SKILL.md instructs users to import a `dialogue_graph` module (`from dialogue_graph import Graph, Node, Edge`), but the bundle only provides `dialogue-graph/scripts/dialogue_graph.py` and does not define an installable/importable `dialogue_graph` package/module at the documented import path. This makes the documented usage likely to fail without extra, undocumented PYTHONPATH/package setup.

locations.section: File location / module name mismatch relative to documented `from dialogue_graph import ...`

description: `Graph.validate()` is advertised as validating graph integrity, but it only checks edge endpoint existence and does not validate key constraints that the task/evaluators commonly enforce (e.g., all nodes reachable from the first node). Using this validation as-is can allow structurally invalid graphs to pass "validate" while failing downstream constraints.

The implementation treats the special target `"End"` inconsistently across validation/serialization/visualization: `validate()` explicitly allows edges to point to `End` even when `End` is not present in `self.nodes`, `to_dict()`/`to_json()` will omit an `End` node unless the user added one, but `visualize()` always injects an `End` node into the DOT output. This can produce a JSON graph with dangling `to: "End"` references (depending on consumer expectations) and a DOT graph that does not faithfully represent the serialized JSON graph.
